mechaber.en:
If one takes a vow to fast on a certain day, and he
then forgets and eats, he should still complete the fast. This applies to dream fasts, public fasts, or days that he knows to fast on like the day that his father or rabbi died. But if he vows to fast one or two days, and he forgets and eats a kezayit, he has "lost" his fast, and he must fast another day. (Rem"a: There are those who are stringent, saying that when he vowed to fast on a specific day, he is obligated to finish the fast but still must be stringent and fast another day (Trumat Hadeshen chapter 156)). Another day. If he accepted upon himself to fast two consecutive days and forgot and ate at night, he fasts two other days. Kol Bo; Beit Yosef siman 572.
They are stringent. The reason is that some say that even on this day he is permitted to borrow the fast and repay it; therefore, when he ate, he lost his fast and is obligated to fast another day. Thus they are stringent like both views: he must fast that entire day and also another day. But on a fixed fast, when it is forbidden to eat, he does not need to fast another day unless his intention is atonement for his sin and inadvertence. Terumat HaDeshen; Magen Avraham.

(כ) להתענות וכו' - ואם חל יום ל"א של לידת בנו בשבת שצריך לעשות הפדיון ביום א' דהוא פדיון שלא בזמנו מסתפק המ"א אם הוי סעודת מצוה ומותר לאכול כשחל בעשי"ת או לא (ואינו דומה לברית מילה דהוי סעודת מצוה אף שלא בזמנו דהתם כל שעתא ושעתא זמניה הוא כדי שלא יהיה ערל משא"כ לענין פדיון הבן) וע"כ מצדד דיעשה הסעודה אח"כ בלילה [ובדגול מרבבה כתב דטוב יותר שיעשה הפדיון והסעודה בליל מוצאי שבת ע"ש] וכתב הרמ"א דכל זה דוקא בכהאי גוונא אבל בשאר תענית שגוזרים הצבור אסור לאכול אף בסעודת מצוה. וע"כ אם חל פדיון הבן ביום ת"צ אף שנוהגים לפדותו ביום התענית הסעודה אין עושין ביום כ"א אח"כ בלילה [מ"א] ובהגהת חתם סופר מצדד דאף בזה יעשה הפדיון והסעודה בליל כניסת יום ל"א ע"ש. עוד כתב המ"א צ"ע כשמתענים כ' סיון במלכות פולין אם מותר לאכול על סעודת מצוה [דאפשר דהוא בכלל שאר ת"צ דאסור וכנ"ל] ומיהו בזמנינו ע"פ הרוב עושין כל הסעודות בלילה ומיהו פ"א חל כ' סיון בע"ש והיה סעודת ברית מילה וצוה הרב לאכול ביום מפני שלא ימצאו אנשים שילכו בלילה. ובעיר שאין מתענין כ' סיון ויש שם אנשים ממקומות שמתענין אם צריכין להשלים למנין מותרים לאכול אפילו בכל הימים [ח"א]:
(כא) ואם קבל עליו וכו' - ר"ל דכל זה דוקא כשלא קבל עליו התענית אלא שסמך עצמו על המנהג או שענה אמן כשמברכין בה"ב דאז לא קיבל עליו בנדר ואם רצה שלא להתענות רשאי ולכן אפילו לא ידע שיזמינו אותו לסעודה והתחיל להתענות מ"מ מותר לאכול בסעודת מצוה אבל אם קיבל עליו התענית במנחה שעשה יותר ממנהג צריך לקיים ולהתענות אף בסעודת מצוה [לבוש] ודעת המ"א ואיזה אחרונים דאף כשקיבל עליו במנחה מותר כיון שקבלתו היה עבור המנהג ורמ"א מיירי במי שאינו מתענה כל בה"ב או כל עשי"ת אלא שמתענה יום או יומיים ונמצא דזה צריך מדינא לקבל במנחה ודינו כאלו מתענה באמצע השנה שהרי אינו תלוי במנהג וע"כ חייב להתענות. והנה מהגר"א משמע שמפרש כהלבוש ומ"מ נראה דבזה יכול ללות ולפרוע תענית אחרת דבלא"ה יש כמה ראשונים דס"ל דאפילו באומר הרני מקבל להתענות למחר יכול ללות ולפרוע:
(כב) בתעניתו - היינו בתענית יחיד אבל תענית שגוזרים הצבור לא מהני פדיון אם לא שהתנו כן הצבור:
(כג) יכול לפדותו וכו' - משום דאומדן דעתא דאדעתא דהכי קיבל דתענית נחשב לצדקה וכיון שנותן דמי חלבו ודמו לעניים יצא:
(כד) בממון - ושיעור הפדיון העשיר לפי עשרו דהטעם משום ששקול צער הממון נגד צער התענית וע"כ בכל אחד לפי מה שהוא:
(כה) בקיבל עליו תענית בעלמא - ר"ל ולא ייחד בשעת הקבלה לאיזה יום דבייחד שאמר אז הרני בתענית למחר דינו כנודר ליום זה וכנ"ל בס"ב ועיין בבה"ל:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(9) For a mitzvah matter - such as for a brit milah or a siyum of a tractate, even if he has no personal connection to it. Nevertheless, in all such cases he must fast part of the day, a little longer than his usual time; for example, if he usually eats in the fourth hour, he should eat in the fifth hour. Some say that even if they pressed him to attend a friendly celebration it is permitted, because of the ways of peace. But from the wording of the Shulchan Aruch, which says "because of the honor of a great person," it implies that this applies specifically for the honor of one who presses him, but not for other people.
(10) He borrows and repays, etc. - And he does not need to annul the vow.
(11) At the beginning of the vow - Meaning, even though he accepted it yesterday at Minchah, that acceptance is not now considered the beginning of the vow; rather, the beginning was when he first resolved to fast on some day, and there he did not specify the day.
(12) This is called this fast and is not, etc. - See the Taz, whose view is that if he is distressed by his fast and has fasted part of the day, he may borrow and repay with another day even on this very day. But the view of the Magen Avraham and several later authorities is that he may borrow and repay only where he accepted a fast in general terms, and even there only if he has fasted part of the day, as above.
(13) Monday and Thursday the whole year - For this is considered a designated day, and he cannot exchange it for other days. Nor can he move it to another year, for since he said "this year," he meant this year specifically. But if he vowed to fast Monday-Thursday-Monday for half a year or a year and did not say "this year," it is not called "this day," and he may borrow and repay on other Monday-Thursday-Monday days after the first half-year or year has ended. But he may not exchange them for other days, such as Sunday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Friday, for perhaps he was particular about these days specifically, since they are days of favor. The later authorities wrote that one who vowed to fast Monday-Thursday-Monday may exchange them and fast Thursday-Monday-Thursday, for his intention was only these days, which are days of favor.
(14) A fast for a dream - Or a yahrtzeit.
(15) Even during the Ten Days of Repentance - Meaning, since these days in particular are designated, one might have thought that eating is forbidden.
(16) A brit milah - Or pidyon haben, or another seudat mitzvah.
(17) A mitzvah, etc. - And he does not need to fast another day because of this.
(18) To eat - It is obvious that where it is permitted to eat at the meal, it is not a fast at all, and afterward he may drink and eat even at home. However, before the meal he may not eat or drink at home. The baalei brit, however, may eat and drink immediately, for it is their Yom Tov. In Eliyah Rabbah he is uncertain whether this is perhaps only after Minchah; see there.
(19) For they did not practice, etc. - If before Rosh Hashanah he knows that between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur he will eat at a brit milah or another seudat mitzvah, he is obligated to fast one additional day before Rosh Hashanah, for this is the reason they fast four days before Rosh Hashanah, corresponding to the four days on which they eat. All the more so if the seudat mitzvah occurs during the four days before Rosh Hashanah, he should fast one day in its place. However, if Rosh Hashanah falls on Thursday, so that there are only four days before Rosh Hashanah, he need not fast one day before Shabbat, for from the outset they accepted only to fast on the days of Selichot and not on other days.
(20) To fast, etc. - If the thirty-first day from his son's birth falls on Shabbat, so that the pidyon must be done on Sunday and is a delayed pidyon, the Magen Avraham is uncertain whether it counts as a seudat mitzvah and one may eat when it falls during the Ten Days of Repentance. It is not comparable to brit milah, which is a seudat mitzvah even when delayed, for there every hour is its time so that he not remain uncircumcised, unlike pidyon haben. Therefore he inclines that the meal should be made afterward at night. In Dagul Merevavah he wrote that it is better to make the pidyon and the meal on Motzaei Shabbat; see there. The Rama wrote that all this applies only in such a case, but on other fasts decreed by the community it is forbidden to eat even at a seudat mitzvah. Therefore, if a pidyon haben falls on a public fast day, although the practice is to redeem him on the fast day, the meal is not made that day but afterward at night, as the Magen Avraham writes. In the gloss of Chatam Sofer he inclines that even in this case the pidyon and the meal should be made on the night entering the thirty-first day; see there. The Magen Avraham further wrote that it requires study when they fast on 20 Sivan in the kingdom of Poland whether one may eat at a seudat mitzvah, for perhaps it is included among other public fasts where it is forbidden, as above. In our times, however, most such meals are made at night. Once 20 Sivan fell on Friday and there was a brit milah meal, and the rabbi ordered them to eat by day because people would not be found to go at night. In a city where they do not fast on 20 Sivan, and people from places that do fast are present there, if they are needed to complete a minyan they may eat even on all the days, as Chayei Adam writes.
(21) And if he accepted upon himself, etc. - Meaning that all this applies only when he did not accept the fast upon himself, but merely relied on the custom, or answered amen when Monday-Thursday-Monday was blessed, in which case he did not accept it as a vow and may choose not to fast. Therefore, even if he did not know that he would be invited to a meal and began to fast, he may nevertheless eat at a seudat mitzvah. But if he accepted the fast upon himself at Minchah, doing more than the custom, he must fulfill it and fast even at a seudat mitzvah, according to Levush. The Magen Avraham and some later authorities hold that even when he accepted it at Minchah it is permitted, since his acceptance was because of the custom; and the Rama is speaking of one who does not fast all Monday-Thursday-Monday or all the Ten Days of Repentance, but only one or two days, so he must by law accept at Minchah, and his status is like one fasting in the middle of the year, since it does not depend on custom, and therefore he must fast. From the Gra it seems that he explains like the Levush. Nevertheless, it appears that in such a case he may borrow and repay another fast, for in any event several Rishonim hold that even one who says, "I accept upon myself to fast tomorrow," may borrow and repay.
(22) With his fast - This means an individual's fast. But for a fast decreed by the community, redemption does not help unless the community stipulated so.
(23) He may redeem it, etc. - For we estimate that he accepted it with this in mind: the fast is considered tzedakah, and since he gives the value of his fat and blood to the poor, he has fulfilled it.
(24) With money - The measure of redemption for a wealthy person is according to his wealth, for the reason is that the distress of the money is weighed against the distress of the fast; therefore each person gives according to what he is.
(25) When he accepted a fast in general - Meaning that at the time of acceptance he did not specify a particular day. If he did specify, saying then, "I am in a fast tomorrow," his law is like one who vows for this day, as above in seif 2; see Biur Halacha.

mechaber.en: There is one who says that fasting for two days and two nights consecutively is equal to forty non-consecutive fasts. Rem"a: There are those who say that for a weak person, two consecutive consecutive days if sufficient, but for a healthy person, three is necessary (Mahar"i Brynn's notes on customs). It seems to me that all of this applies only to somebody who must fast for forty non-consecutive days for repentance in order to cause himself pain. In those cases, we equate this pain to that pain, and that is why the later authorities discuss this. However, somebody who vows to fast forty days must fulfill his vow, because it isn't any weaker than saying "this day," where he cannot borrow and repay. Even those who hold that when he says "this day," he can borrow and repay, would concede here that he must fulfill his vow. This applies even more to the forty days before Yom Kippur when people fast in remembrance of Moses's ascent of the Mountain [Sinai]. One who has accepted these cannot repay them with two or three consecutive days.

beur_hagra.en:
(א) Seif 67, when it occurred, etc. As in Nedarim and he knew the year was intercalated. Mahari Weil siman 5, brought in Beit Yosef — this is Rambam's method who ruled like R' Meir in Nedarim 63 and as Abaye established there that the anonymous mishnah is R' Meir, as in Shulchan Aruch Yoreh Deah siman 220 in his name; but all poskim disagreed, as Rosh and Ran there that halachah is like R' Yehudah, and so ruled in Shulchan Aruch there and Choshen Mishpat siman 43 paragraph 28, and Orach Chayim beginning siman 528 in the gloss, and Even HaEzer siman 126 seif 7 in the gloss; and this is what the Rav wrote "some say," etc.; so too in Turei David siman 294 and Maharil siman 31; Maharil also wrote proof from chapter 1 of Megillah that if not for connecting redemption to redemption it would be reasonable to do in the first [Adar], except he wrote one may say there it is because we do not pass over mitzvot; in Turei David he also brought this proof and wrote because we do not pass over mitzvot, and the same we do not pass over, etc.; he wrote there later "I saw," etc., and these are Maharil's words there and he did not heed his words. But all their proofs do not seem right to me, for from Nedarim there is no proof, for there they disagree about people's language — in Nedarim we follow people's language, and so in documents; but here the essence is fasting in both months; for Rabbenu Gershom one need not establish Tosefta in Megillah 6b except regarding order of portions, but otherwise he agrees to Tosefta that all mitzvot practiced in the second are practiced in the first; so too in Megillat Taanit chapter 2 which lists Megillat Taanit of Adar — it is written there there is no difference between first and second Adar except reading Megillah and sending gifts to the poor; so I saw in Magen Avraham who brought this proof; although he wrote Rabbenu Gershom says all mitzvot practiced in the second are not in the first except eulogy and fasting forbidden in both — we hold like Rabbenu Gershom; nevertheless he said except eulogy and fasting, meaning all mentioned in Megillat Taanit refers to that, and the same for fasting as in the Gemara there is no difference except order of portions that must be near Nisan; so in the Gemara "and the same for eulogy," etc., refers to all prohibitions of that month; Tosafot there s.v. R' Elazar, etc., 14 and 15 in first Adar — although forbidden in eulogy and fasting, one need not make feast and joy; at first glance it is difficult, for we derive prohibition of eulogy and fasting from feast and joy; but per this it fits that the reason eulogy and fasting are forbidden in the first is not because the verse forbids only in the second as "the second," but because they are written in Megillat Taanit as in Megillat Taanit and Gemara there 5b, and it is written there in Megillat Taanit there is no difference between first Adar, etc., as above; afterward it is written they write in a document "first Adar," etc., as in end of chapter Konom — plainly documents are a different dispute. Second proof they brought from Megillah that Rabbenu Gershom's reason is because of redemption, etc. — is not proof, for certainly per their view who hold one month alone it is proof, but the Gemara there proves as written they practice in both, since it challenges Rabbenu Gershom's reason and does not challenge Tosefta who practices in both — we learn the presumption is to practice in both, only after they learned from each year it is practiced in only one; as written "if the second were announced," etc., it challenges: granted, etc., but, etc.; therefore they need not in each year, whether R' Yehudah or Rabbenu Gershom, except to exclude Tosefta who should not practice in both — to exclude first or second we do not learn from Scripture, only for this because we do not pass over, and for that because "the second" is written; but Magen Avraham's proof from "if the second were announced" does not seem different because "the second" is written — on the contrary from this it would seem to practice in the first; but what I wrote is a clear proof, and what Magen Avraham wrote from end of chapter 2 of Taanit regarding Nikanor day and Turinus day is a clear proof, and from what is written it was needed only for an intercalated month — although the essence is like Rashi's second explanation there and Tosafot there explained; nevertheless from not answering otherwise we learn it was needed only for an intercalated year — we learn it applies in the second too, as Megillat Taanit states explicitly, and so Mahari Weil there that Maharil so ruled, and he ruled so; see Shach Yoreh Deah siman 220 note 8 that many later authorities hold like Rambam and wrote that in Nedarim too one should be strict in both months, all the more here where it is the law.

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ז] ברית מילה וכו'. והוא הדין פדיון הבן או שאר סעודת מצוה ואם חל יום שלושים ואחד בשבת וביום ראשון הוא תענית הנזכר לעיל יעשה הסעודה בלילה, אבל מילה אף שלא בזמנה עושה ביום כשמתענין כ' סיון במדינת פולין עושין הסעודה בלילה אם לא שחל בערב שבת, אבל בשאר תענית שגוזרין הציבור אסור לאכול אפילו בסעודת מצוה (מגן אברהם). עוד כתב במקום דמותר אסור לאכול קודם הסעודה בביתו אם לא בעלי ברית דמותרים מיד לאכול דיום טוב שלהם הוא אבל אחר שאכל בסעודה מותר לכולם אפילו בביתו, עד כאן, וצריך עיון מסוף סימן תקנ"ט דאף בעל ברית אין מותר אלא אחר תפילת מנחה והוא מש"ס ואפשר בתעניתים אלו קיל יותר מתשעה באב שנדחה, ותדע דהא לקמן אסור לעשות סעודה אי נמי דהכי קאמר מותרים מיד אחר מנחה אף קודם הסעודה:

magen_avraham.he: באדר שני. דדמי למי שנדר עד אדר דאם ידע שהשנה מעוברת אסור עד אדר שני וה"נ הוא ידע (ב"י מהרי"ו) וקשה דהרב"י כתב בי"ד סי' ר"כ ס"ח דלהרמב"ם הוי דינא הכי אבל רוב הפוסקים ס"ל דאפי' ידע שהיא מעוברת הוי עד אדר ראשון ועוד ק' התינח אם שנה ראשונה לא היתה מעוברת והתחיל להתענות באדר אז דמי לנדר אבל אם שנה ראשונה מעוברת ובא לימלך באיזה אדר יתענה היאך נעשה ול"נ להביא ראיה מדאמרי' בתענית דף י"ח ע"א לחדש מעובר ופרש"י דהשנה מעובר' כו' משמע להדיא דנוהג באדר שני וגם אמרי' התם ע"ב דיום טוריינוס ויום נקנור כלם נוהגין באדר שני דאלת"ה לא פריך מידי מפורים ע"ש א"כ גם יום שמת בו אביו יש לנהוג בשני ובת"ה מביא ראיה לנהוג בראשון מדאמרי' פ"ק דמגילה דקריאת המגילה בשני משום דמסמך גאולה לגאולה עדיף משמע דאי לאו האי טעמא עבדי' בראשון ע"ש ובתשו' מהרי"ל סי' ל"א דחה ראי' זו משום דבמגילה ס"ד למיעבד בראשון דאין מעבירין על המצו' ע"כ ובגמ' משמע דאי לאו קרא הוי עבדי' פורים בתרוויהו ע"ש ואפשר דגם ימים הכתובים במ"ת נהגו בשניהם וכ"מ קצת בס"ס מ"ת שכת' אין בין אדר ראשון לאדר השני אלא מקרא מגילה וכו' משמע שבא לאורויי שכל הימים הכתובים במ"ת נהגו בשניהם ועוד די"ד וט"ו אסורים בהספד ותעני' בשניהן לכן מדינא יש להתענות בשניהם אך כיון שיום שמת בו אביו אינו אלא מנהג א"צ לעשות אלא כמו שנהג בתחלה דמעיקרא אדעתא דהכי קביל עליה אבל מי שנדר להתענות יום שמת בו רבו וכדומה צריך להתענו' בשניהם כנ"ל ועבי"ד סי' ת"ב בש"כ וט"ז ובכ"ה בשם הר"ש הלוי סי"ו כתב דיש להתענו' בראשון ובס"ח סי' תשי"ב כת' א' מת אביו באדר ראשון והיה מתענה בשנה פשוטה בשבט ובאדר עכ"ל ול"נ דלכ"ע האבלים א"צ ליתן לו קדיש אלא פעם א' וכיוצא בזה כתב במט"מ בשם רש"ל מי שאינו יודע יום שמת בו אביו יברור לו יום א' אך אל יסיג גבול לומר קדיש, ומי שמת אביו ביום ראשון דר"ח כסלו ולשנה הבאה חשון חסר ור"ח כסלו אינו אלא יום א' צ"ע מתי יתענה אם בכ"ט לחשון שהוא יום א' לפני ר"ח כסליו דהא לעול' יום שני עיקר שמונין מועדות משני או נימא דעכ"פ הוי שם ר"ח עליו ולכן יתענה בר"ח ובא"ע סי' קכ"ו יש דיעות אם יום ל' נמנה לחדש העבר או להבא ונ"ל דאם שנה ראשונה היא חסרה יקבע בכ"ט לחשון דבאמת משמע בגמרא דנדרים דיום ל' הוא נמנה לחדש העבר (עמ"ש סי' נ"ה ס"י) אבל כששנה ראשונה היא ג"כ מלאה א"כ צריך ליקבע היום בר"ח ולכן אף בשנים הבאים אחריהם אף שהם חסרים יקבע בר"ח דה"ל כמו נדר דאזלי' אחר לשון בני אדם כמ"ש מהרי"ל ומהרי"ו ועבי"ד סי' ר"כ, ואם מת ביום ראשון דר"ח אדר יתענה לשנה הבאה ביום ראשון דר"ח אדר ראשון ולא בכ"ט בו דלעולם אדר ראשון עומד תחת אדר שני:
magen_avraham.en: In second Adar. Like one who vowed until Adar — if he knew the year was intercalated he is forbidden until second Adar, and the same here he knew (Beit Yosef, Mahari Weil). It is difficult, for Rabbenu Yerucham wrote Yoreh Deah siman 220 note 8 that for Rambam this is the law, but most poskim hold even if he knew it is intercalated it is until first Adar; moreover it is resolved if the first year was not intercalated and he began fasting in Adar — then like a vow; but if the first year was intercalated and he comes to consult which Adar to fast — how is it done? In my humble opinion bring proof from Taanit 18a for an intercalated month — Rashi explained the year was intercalated, etc. — implying explicitly practiced in second Adar; they also said there 2b that Turinus day and Nikanor day are all practiced in second Adar — otherwise it would immediately challenge from Purim, see there; so too yahrzeit day one practices in both, and Turei David brings proof to practice in the first from chapter 1 Megillah that Megillah reading in the second is because connecting redemption to redemption is preferable — implying if not for that reason they would do in the first, see there; in responsa Maharil siman 31 he rejected this proof because in Megillah presumably they would do in the first because we do not pass over mitzvot — therefore in Gemara it implies if not for the verse they would do Purim in both, see there; perhaps days written in Megillat Taanit were practiced in both, as somewhat in end of Megillat Taanit “there is no difference between first and second Adar except Megillah reading,” etc. — implying all days written in Megillat Taanit were in both; also 14 and 15 are forbidden in eulogy and fasting in both — therefore by law one fasts in both; but since yahrzeit is only custom one need only do as initially accepted; but one who vowed to fast on his teacher's death day and the like must fast in both as above, see Pri Megadim siman 502 in Shach and Taz and in Knesset HaGedolah in the name of R' Shlomo HaLevi note 16 wrote one fasts in the first, and in Eshel Avraham siman 512 wrote if father died in first Adar he fasted in a plain year in Shevat and Adar, end — in my humble opinion for all mourners he need not be given Kaddish only once, etc., as Mateh Moshe in the name of R' Shlomo Luria for one who does not know father's death day — clarify one day but do not exceed saying Kaddish; one whose father died on first day of Rosh Chodesh Kislev and next year Cheshvan is short and Rosh Chodesh Kislev is only one day — requires study when he fasts if on 29 Cheshvon which is day before his Kislev Rosh Chodesh, for always the second day is primary for counting seasons from the second, or we say at least Rosh Chodesh is upon him and he fasts on Rosh Chodesh; in Even HaEzer siman 126 there are views whether thirty days count to intercalated month or the coming one — it seems if the first year was short he fixes 29 Cheshvon, for truly in Gemara Nedarim thirty days count to the intercalated month (see siman 55 seif 10); but when the first year was also full he must fix the day on Rosh Chodesh, and therefore in later years even if short he fixes on Rosh Chodesh as a vow following people's language as Maharil and Mahari Weil, see Pri Megadim Yoreh Deah siman 220; if he died on first day of Rosh Chodesh Adar he fasts next year on first day of first Adar Rosh Chodesh and not on 29 of it, for first Adar always stands in place of second Adar.

mishnah_berurah.he:
(מא) שמת אביו או אמו - ר"ל שבשנה שמת בו אביו לא היה השנה מעוברת ובשנים הבאים אח"כ איתרמי שנה מעוברת דעת המחבר דסתם אדר הוא אדר שני וי"א להיפך וגם יש בענינינו טעם דאין מעבירין על המצות:
(מב) מיהו יש מחמירין להתענות בשניהם - עיין במ"א שמסיק דאם קבל עליו בנדר להתענות יום שמת בו אביו או רבו מחוייב להתענות בשניהם דכן הוא העיקר לדינא [וכ"כ הגר"א] אכן אם לא קבל עליו בפירוש רק מצד מנהגא שמנהג להתענות יום שמת בו אביו ואמו א"צ להתנהג לעולם אלא כמו שנהג בפעם ראשונה כשמתרמי לו השנה מעוברת דמעיקרא אדעתא דהכי קבל עליה אכן בפעם ראשונה גופא אם בא לימלך כיצד לעשות הנכון לומר לו שיתענה בשניהם (אכן אם קשה לו להתענות בשניהם נראה שטוב יותר שיברור לו יום ראשון דכן הוא המנהג) אכן האבלים אין צריכין ליתן לו קדיש אלא פ"א וכיוצא בזה כתבו בשם רש"ל מי שאינו יודע יום שמת בו אביו ואמו יברור לו יום אחד אך אל יסיג גבול אחרים לומר קדיש. אם מת אביו ביום ראשון דר"ח אדר שני יתענה לשנה הבאה שהיתה שנה פשוטה ביום א' דר"ח אדר ולא בכ"ט בו דלעולם אדר של שנה פשוטה עומד תחת אדר שני של שנה מעוברת. ומי שמת אביו ביום ראשון דר"ח כסליו ולשנה הבאה היה חשוון חסר ור"ח כסליו אינו אלא יום אחד צ"ע מתי יתענה אם בכ"ט לחשוון שהוא יום א' לפני ר"ח כסליו דהא לעולם יום שני עיקר שמונין למועדות משני וא"כ היה יום פטירת אביו יום אחרון מחודש חשוון וגם עתה יקבע ביום אחרון לחודש זה או נימא דעכ"פ הוי שם ר"ח עליו ולכן יקבע יום היא"צ עתה ג"כ בר"ח [ולא להתענות בו דהא אין מתענין בר"ח כדלקמיה אלא להדליק בו נר ולומר קדיש] ומסיק המ"א דאם שנה ראשונה למיתת אביו השנה היא חסרה וכמש"כ וא"כ עדיין לא הוקבע הענין עליו בנדר יקבע היא"צ בכ"ט לחודש חשוון וכמש"כ הטעם אבל כששנה הראשונה היא ג"כ מלאה א"כ צריך ליקבע היום בר"ח ולכן אף בשנים הבאים אחריהם אף שהם חסרים יקבע בר"ח ויש מאחרונים שסוברין דלעולם יקבע בר"ח והעולם נוהגין כהמ"א:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(א) His father or mother died in the year when his father died, and in the coming years, he was not a passing year “And I will be on the other hand, and there is also a taste for our people:

(ב) (b) Who is aggravated to be tortured in both of them - see the M.S.A. who has given him a vow to claim a day in which his father or his rabbi is obligated to answer his behalf He is the most important thing to do with his father and his mother the Omnipresent, but as it was for the first time when you hit him this year, I'll know that Ya'a Dachi had received it for the first time, if I had come to the king because I'm king A side to do the right to say to him that he will respond to both of them (if it is difficult for him to argue with them, it seems better to be clear to him Sunday is the custom) The mourners do not need to give him a devotee, but rather a p.m., who does not know a day when his father and his mother will be clear to him one day Do not reach any other limits to say a devotee.
